messages:
kevin: quick heads-up, onboarding sparrow-lite-int8 to structured-output. Canary is failing JSON schema checks intermittently. Root cause seems to be non-atomic serializer + retry merge leaving stray separators. Sample from canary logs below.

lee: how often? paste sample pls.

kevin: ~0.4% of requests. here's a post-merge buffer we got right before the consumer parse error:

```
... "tool_calls": [ { "id": "c1", "name": "extract", "args": {"q":"summary"} }, , { "id": "c2", "name": "search" ... } ] ...
```

(the double-comma between objects causes JSON parse failure).

sophia: double-comma implies serializer wrote a separator then a retry reset buffer but left separator flag set. Are retries using the same write path?

kevin: yes — retries currently call serializer.append_partial() then serializer.reset_for_retry() but reset doesn't clear pending_separator boolean. If retry emits nothing, we end up with ", ,".

tomas: hmm — similar class of bugs we've seen with streaming batch merges. Two fixes: make serializer transactional (don't emit separator until append confirmed) or force retry to emit a tombstone token that the serializer recognizes and clears separators. Transactional seems cleaner.

lee: transactional serializer + server-side dedupe by tool_call.id would be good. Dedupe protects customers if something slips through. Also add a small TTL-ed set for IDs to avoid memory blowup.

kevin: agreed. Proposed action:
1) short-term: add NDJSON sanity check in canary: run linter after serialization, fail canary if malformed. That's in eng-ml/canary-checks/ndjson_lint.sh
2) short-term: change serializer to emit separators only after append success (PR in progress)
3) medium-term: dedupe tool_call objects by id before final emit (TTL 60s)
4) telemetry: increment structured_malformed_count{model,quant,route,canary_id} and tag duplicate_tool_call=true when detected

sophia: small note: some consumers expect array semantics (JSON array of tool_calls) while others prefer NDJSON streaming. Ensure serializer can emit both safely. Maybe add a mode that forces atomic array assembly for structured-output routes and only streams raw tokens for plain text routes.

tomas: agree. For structured-output we should avoid chunk-level interleaving: either reassemble whole array server-side or provide sequence metadata so clients can reorder. Which is easier here?

kevin: easiest short-term is server-side reassembly for structured-output models on canary. We'll disable streaming for those model+route combos via feature-flag. Longer term we add x-stream-seq headers and per-stream reordering.

devbot: Created ticket INF-3478 and linked to recent canary alerts. Assigned to kevin and lee. https://internal/ops/INF-3478 :white_check_mark:

lee: PR notes: ensure serializer.reset_for_retry() clears separator state and any trailing comma buffer. Also write unit tests that fuzz append->reset sequences and assert JSON validity. I'll add streaming_interleave_fuzz CI test.

sophia: add canary regression gate: if structured_malformed_count > 0 for a model/quant in N runs, block rollout and alert eng-ml. We should catch regressions before customer exposure.

kevin: ack. I'll push the PR with transactional change + ndjson linter in canary. Also will upload repro script: eng-ml/canary-repro/txn-retry-repro.sh which simulates concurrent decoder wartime retries.

tomas: one more thought — we should also consider idempotency tokens for tool_call emissions from model so duplicate detection can be end-to-end (model-generated ids + aggregator-supplied correlation id). But that's a design doc. I'll open RFC.

kevin: perfect. thanks all :thumbsup: I'll update infra with the feature-flag to disable structured streaming on the canary clusters till the fix lands.
